item.content:encoded:
Brazilian Jiu-Jitsu & Submission Grappling

  • Diego 'Pato' Leaves Belt on the Mat After Historic 5th IBJJF World Title
    The 2026 IBJJF World Championships (May 28–31, Long Beach, CA) closed the gi season with several landmark performances. Diego 'Pato' Oliveira captured his record-breaking fifth light-featherweight world title — surpassing the previous mark of four held by his coach Guilherme Mendes — and then retired on the spot by leaving his black belt on the mat. Gabrieli Pessanha swept both the super-heavyweight and absolute women's divisions to claim her 12th world title, becoming the most decorated female competitor in IBJJF history. Tainan Dalpra and Mayssa Bastos also added to their title counts, and teen brown-belt prodigy Hazel Butcher-Salazar went six-for-six by submission before being promoted to black belt on the podium.
    Source: MMA Mania

Global & European Soccer (Atlético Madrid emphasis)

  • Atlético Close In on Grimaldo with Personal Terms Agreed, Club-to-Club Fee Gap Remains
    Atlético Madrid have agreed personal terms with Bayer Leverkusen left-back Alejandro Grimaldo (30), with Fabrizio Romano confirming the player has 'said yes to Atlético's project' on a deal to 2029 plus an option year. The move accelerated after Marc Cucurella chose Real Madrid, leaving Atlético to focus entirely on Grimaldo. The clubs are now haggling over the transfer fee: Atlético have tabled roughly €25m while Leverkusen are holding out for around €30m, though Grimaldo's contract running only to 2027 — and his stated refusal to extend — limits the German club's leverage. Meanwhile, Atlético have a club-record 12 players representing six nations at the 2026 FIFA World Cup, headlined by Julián Álvarez with Argentina.
    Source: Yahoo Sports / Football Espana

Financial Freedom & Markets

  • Apple Confirms iPhone Price Hikes Are Coming as AI-Driven RAM Shortage Bites
    Apple CEO Tim Cook told the Wall Street Journal that price increases on iPhones, Macs, and iPads are 'unavoidable,' driven by a global DRAM shortage fueled by surging AI infrastructure demand. Analysts forecast the iPhone 18 Pro could cost roughly $35 more per unit due to the shift to 2nm chips, with total chip costs rising to ~$85 per handset. Separately, President Trump announced on June 18 that Apple and Intel have agreed to partner on designing and building chips domestically, sending Intel stock up more than 10% — though neither Apple nor Intel has formally confirmed the deal. For investors, VTI has gained approximately 11.5% year-to-date as markets broadly rallied on the U.S.–Iran peace agreement and falling oil prices, though a key upcoming catalyst is the Federal Reserve's next rate decision.
    Source: CNN Business
  • VTI Up ~11.5% YTD as Iran Peace Deal Lifts Stocks and Oil Falls
    The Vanguard Total Stock Market ETF (VTI) has gained approximately 11.5% year-to-date and roughly 25.6% over the past year, buoyed recently by a U.S.–Iran peace agreement that sent oil prices lower and lifted broad equity markets. VTI holds over 3,450 stocks with $650 billion in total assets, with top positions in Nvidia (6.6%), Apple (5.7%), and Microsoft (4.4%). Investors are now watching for the Federal Reserve's next rate decision and monitoring whether the AI-driven memory chip crisis will pressure consumer tech prices further — a risk that is especially relevant for AAPL, which hit an all-time high of $317.40 on June 8 before pulling back slightly. For families and homeowners in NJ, the broader market strength is a tailwind for long-term index fund portfolios, though rising Apple device prices are an upcoming household cost to plan for.
    Source: TipRanks / TradingView

NJ Local News (Montclair emphasis)

  • Montclair Launches Summer Pedestrian Plaza and World Cup Soccer Watch Parties
    Montclair has announced a new pedestrian-only zone on Church Street for upcoming summer and fall weekends, giving families a car-free downtown space to enjoy. Soccer fans of all ages have a dedicated hub at Lackawanna Station, where 'Summer of Soccer' is running 39 consecutive days of free watch parties and tournament play tied to the 2026 FIFA World Cup — perfect for a 12-year-old soccer fan. On the food scene, popular local spot Jackie's Grillette is expanding in Montclair, while beloved Uncle Momo is set to close later this month after 15 years. Montclair Film's outdoor 'Movie Night Under the Stars' series also kicked off June 14, offering free films for families through the summer.
    Source: The Montclair Girl
  • Montclair Public Library Scores $36.6M NJ Tax Credit for Major Redevelopment
    The Montclair Public Library has received a $36.6 million tax credit award from the New Jersey Economic Development Authority to support a significant redevelopment of the building. The funding is expected to modernize the library into a larger community resource — a big win for families and students in town. Separately, Governor Mikie Sherrill signed legislation requiring public schools to prominently post free and reduced-price meal application information online, and announced $120 Summer EBT benefits for more than 680,000 eligible New Jersey students.
    Source: The Montclair Girl
